For a renter, I’d start with the **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W solar panel kit**. It’s a compact, no-wiring setup: place the panel on your balcony when the sun’s out, bring it inside afterward, and use the battery station indoors. It’s suited to phones, a laptop, router, or fan—not a fridge or heater. The listed capacity is 288 Wh, so expect to prioritize smaller devices. [Kit details and current listed price](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-for-an-apartment-balcony) · [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2-100w-solar-kit)

Check your lease and building rules before putting a panel on the balcony, and make sure it’s secured safely. This kind of kit charges a portable battery; it **doesn’t feed power into your apartment’s wiring**. Solar charging will also depend on how much direct sun your balcony gets. [More on the kit’s renter and balcony considerations](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-for-an-apartment-balcony)
